claim_being_audited: The current release can be certified as model-card compliant based on aggregate readiness and rehearsal results, with the merchant dispute regression handled as a disclosed current limitation rather than a blocker.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material merchant dispute weakness is either disclosed or covered by approved mitigation.
Use suspicious when the overall readiness case is plausible but a required policy predicate or support link is missing.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring notes may inform context but cannot satisfy the current-documentation or approved-mitigation requirement.
The conclusion should rest on admissible evidence alone, not on conditional wording that assumes documentation exists outside the record.
evidence_requests: Current release model-card or certification document showing the merchant dispute limitation is explicitly disclosed.
Approved mitigation or formal risk-acceptance record covering the merchant dispute regression before launch, if disclosure is not present.
Current-release documentation tying the cited evaluation results to the certification packet for this launch.
specific_concerns: The policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and to disclose material segment weaknesses unless resolved or covered by approved mitigation.
The admissible record shows a current merchant dispute subgroup regression below the warning threshold for a named launch use case.
No admissible evidence shows that the current release documentation actually includes the required disclosure language.
No approved mitigation or risk acceptance is attached; the monitoring comment is explicitly informal context only.
Prior approval of the same model family is stale context and does not cover the current retrieval change and eval batch.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the current record, rather than only conditionally supportable if disclosure is added.
That the merchant dispute weakness is already adequately handled for policy purposes.
That informal post-launch monitoring is equivalent to approved mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure.
